Why links rot

By Ada Example

Most of the pages people save are gone within a decade. A study of links cited in court opinions found that half of them no longer pointed at the page the judge read, and the share is higher for links shared on social sites.

There are three common causes. A site moves to a new system and its addresses change, the company behind it shuts down, or a single page is edited until it no longer says what it said.

What you can do

  • Keep a copy of the text you care about.
  • Check the Internet Archive for older captures.
    • Search by the exact address.
The web forgets faster than we think it does, and it forgets quietly.
curl -I https://example.com/old-page
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found

None of this needs an account, and none of it needs the page to still exist once the copy is made.
Keep the copies close.
